papers.title: Local crystallization in three-dimensional quantization
papers.abstract: A long-standing conjecture on the quantization problem due to Gersho, which remains open in dimensions higher than two, posits that optimal quantizers crystallize into a lattice structure; in dimension three, the natural candidate is the body-centered cubic (BCC) lattice, known to be optimal among other lattices. In this paper, we establish the asymptotic local optimality of the BCC lattice under small periodic perturbations, extending its known stability beyond the class of lattice configurations. Our approach connects the discrete geometry of Voronoi tessellations with a continuum variational problem, showing that the rescaled quadratic quantization energies converge to a continuum functional describing locally deformed BCC lattices. A central ingredient is a geometric and algebraic framework that combines the stability of the BCC Voronoi structure, a discrete calculus on its adjacency graph and an analysis of the lattice symmetries via representation theory, allowing us to establish the positivity of the second variation at the BCC configuration and thereby prove the local minimality of the BCC lattice for the limiting energy.

papers.title: Sharp boundedness criteria for nonnegative kernels on regular curves in the Heisenberg group
papers.abstract: In this paper we study singular integrals associated with the nonnegative kernels \[ K_\alpha(x,y,z)=\frac{|z|^{\alpha/2}}{\|(x,y,z)\|^{\alpha+1}}, \qquad \alpha>0, \] in the first Heisenberg group $\mathbb H$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Kor\'anyi norm. This family was introduced by Chousionis and Li. We first show that there exists a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve $E\subset\mathbb H$ such that the singular integrals associated with $K_\alpha$ are unbounded on $L^2(E)$ for every $0<\alpha<4$. This extends the counterexamples of Chousionis, Li and Zhang from $0<\alpha<2$ to the full range $0<\alpha<4$. Combined with the boundedness theorem of F\"assler and Orponen for $\alpha\ge4$, our result determines the exact range of exponents for boundedness on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve. We also consider the more general kernels \[ K_\Phi(p)=\frac{1}{\|p\|} \Phi\!\left(\frac{|z|^{1/2}}{\|p\|}\right), \qquad p=(x,y,z)\neq0, \] where $\Phi:[0,1]\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous and nondecreasing, with $\Phi(0)=0$. We show that the associated singular integral is $L^2$-bounded on every $1$-Ahlfors regular curve if and only if $\Phi(u)=O(u^4)$ as $u\to0$. When this condition fails, we construct a compact $1$-Ahlfors regular horizontal $C^1$ curve on which the operator is unbounded. The curves in both constructions can be chosen as horizontal lifts of planar $C^1$ graphs with arbitrarily small slope.

papers.title: Szarek and Ball made simple
papers.abstract: We present proofs of Szarek's moment comparison and Ball's cube slicing inequalities based on elementary convexity and majorisation. The key ingredient is a moment-lifting argument which allows us to use Schur monotonicity, avoiding the integral inequalities used in the original Fourier-analytic approaches.

papers.title: Inscribed 4-polytopes of maximal volume with seven and eight vertices
papers.abstract: We prove, with sum-of-squares certificates checked in exact arithmetic, that every cyclic $4$-polytope with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ has volume at most $2/5$. Hence no $4$-polytope of maximal volume with seven vertices inscribed in $\mathbb{S}^{3}$ is cyclic, answering a question of Horv\'ath and L\'angi for $d = 4$, and with their theorem the maximal volume is $\sqrt{3}/4$. With eight vertices, the same method bounds the volume of every simplicial type other than the cross-polytope by $13/20$, so the regular cross-polytope, of volume $2/3$, is up to orthogonal transformations the unique maximiser.

papers.title: Littlewood's mutually touching cylinders: the maximum is seven
papers.abstract: We give a computer-assisted proof that eight congruent infinite circular cylinders in $\mathbb{R}^3$ cannot touch pairwise. Since seven such cylinders exist, the maximum number of congruent mutually touching infinite cylinders is seven. This answers a question of Littlewood from 1968.

papers.title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
papers.abstract: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.

papers.title: Solid-angle formulas for simplicial cones and random shifted sections of polytopes
papers.abstract: We consider simplicial cones $C = \operatorname{pos}(v_1, \ldots, v_n) \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose generators have a Gram matrix of the form $(\langle v_i, v_j \rangle)_{i,j=1}^n = \operatorname{Id}_n+\sum_{j=1}^p \lambda_j u_j u_j^T$, where $p\in \{0,\ldots, n\}$, $\lambda_1, \ldots, \lambda_p > -1$ and $u_1,\ldots, u_p \in \mathbb{R}^n$ are orthogonal unit vectors. We derive an explicit $p$-dimensional integral formula for the solid angle of $C$ involving the analytic continuation of the standard normal distribution function. As an application, explicit formulas are obtained for the expected face numbers of sections of acute orthocentric simplices and crosspolytopes with uniformly distributed linear subspaces translated by a fixed vector. The translation vector is assumed to lie outside the affine hulls of all proper faces of the polytope. All solid angles entering these formulas are expressed as integrals of dimension at most two. This application includes regular simplices and regular crosspolytopes as special cases.

papers.title: An exact formula for optimal axis-parallel packing of eight squares
papers.abstract: We determine the smallest square container for eight axis-parallel squares of prescribed side lengths. The optimal side length is the minimum of the costs of 23 explicit packing strategies, and each cost is a maximum of sums of side lengths. No minimum of fewer convex functions represents it. Three strategies suffice for seven squares; the jump to 23 for eight squares witnesses the beginning of a combinatorial explosion. We prove the formula by combining the constructions with geometric lower bounds derived from disjoint coordinate projections, cornering arguments, and a weighted area comparison.

papers.title: A Universal Law of Large Numbers for Extreme Cycles in Random \v{C}ech Complexes
papers.abstract: We study the maximal multiplicative persistence of $k$-cycles in random \v{C}ech complexes. Let $f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ be a probability density function, let ${P}_n$ be a Poisson process with intensity $nf$, and let $\Pi_{k,n}$ denote the largest death-to-birth ratio among all non-essential $k$-cycles ($1\le k \le d-1$). For the uniform distribution in the unit hypercube, it was proved in [9] that $\Pi_{k,n} = \Theta\left( \left(\frac{\log n}{\log\log n}\right)^{1/k}\right)$. In this paper we sharpen and extend this result to a law of large numbers, for a broad class of distributions. Most significantly, we show that the limiting constant depends only on $d$ and $k$, and not on the probability density $f$. Thus the extreme value of multiplicative persistence exhibits a universality phenomenon. We show that the limiting constant is determined by the asymptotic covering density of the $k$-dimensional sphere. Our proof identifies the geometric mechanism underlying maximal cycles, a persistent isoperimetric inequality, which gives sharp bounds on the number of points needed to generate a highly persistent cycle. By combining covering-density estimates with isoperimetric inequalities, we show that this minimum is asymptotically attained by efficient coverings of a $k$-sphere. A key ingredient is a geometric measure theory argument that uses compactness to relate discrete covering counts to the volume of a limiting cycle.

papers.title: The Volume Exchange Metric
papers.abstract: The volume exchange metric between cell structures embedded in Euclidean space is introduced. Intuitively, it measures the minimum amount of volume that must be swept out to continuously transform one cell structure into another. The main result is that the volume exchange metric coincides with a discrete analogue defined as a minimum over matchings between cells. Algorithms are described to compute the discrete volume exchange metric and illustrate its effectiveness at distinguishing polycrystalline microstructures in computational experiments.

papers.title: Braid spaces have no geodesic loops
papers.abstract: The braid spaces are defined as universal metric coverings of the standard complex spaces, branched over certain hyperplane arrangements. We describe a natural family of convex functions on braid spaces and use them to prove that braid spaces contain no geodesic loops. This statement is a consequence of the well-known conjecture that every braid space is CAT(0).

papers.title: An orthogonality inequality in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$ and the double-cap conjecture
papers.abstract: The orthogonal neighborhood of a set in real projective space is the union of the hyperplanes perpendicular to its points. We prove that caps minimize neighborhood measure among measurable sets of fixed measure in $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$, for $n \geq 3$, with rigidity up to null sets. This yields the double-cap conjecture: a measurable subset of $S^{n-1}$ containing no orthogonal pair has measure at most that of two opposite open caps of radius $\pi/4$. The argument combines compactness of the Funk transform, rotation comparisons, and projective variations. We also obtain qualitative stability and determine the measurable fractional chromatic number of the spherical orthogonality graph. AI played an assistive role in preparing this paper. The formalization and verification workflow for a separate Lean 4 proof of the main inequality and double-cap result, based on a different argument, were carried out almost entirely using AI-assisted tools.

papers.title: Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families
papers.abstract: We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.

papers.title: Median spaces with the strict separation property and superrigidity of actions
papers.abstract: We introduce strictly separated median spaces, prove structural results and establish superrigidity for actions of higher rank lattices on the latter. We consider two different approach, the first one relies on the construction of a boundary map and the second one is self-contained and relies on the median geometry of the space of sections taking values in a median space.

papers.title: Apollonian carpets and the boundary of the Kahler cone of a hyperkahler manifold
papers.abstract: The ample cone of a compact Kahler $n$-manifold $M$ is the intersection of its Kahler cone and the real subspace generated by integer (1,1)-classes. Its isotropic boundary is the set of all points $\eta$ on its boundary such that $\int_M \eta^n=0$. We are interested in the relation between the shape of the isotropic boundary of the ample cone of a hyperkahler manifold and the dynamics of its holomorphic automorphism group $G$. In this case, the projectivization of the ample cone is realized as an open, locally polyhedral subset in a hyperbolic space $H$. The isotropic boundary $S$ is realized as a subset of the hyperbolic boundary (the absolute) $A$ of $H$, which is naturally identified with a Euclidean sphere. It is clear that the isotropic boundary $S$ contains the limit set of $G$ acting on its ample cone. We prove that, conversely, all irrational points on $S$ belong to the limit set. Using a result of N. Shah about limiting distributions of curves under geodesic flow on hyperbolic manifolds, we prove that every real analytic curve in $S$ is contained in a geodesic sphere in $S$,and in presence of such curves the limit set is the closure of the union of these geodesic spheres. We study the geometry of such fractal sets, called Apollonian carpets, and establish the link between the Apollonian carpet and the structure of the automorphism group.

papers.title: Light rays of Lorentzian graphs and the Born-Infeld model
papers.abstract: Following a program outlined by Bartnik, and also employing nonlinear potential techniques we developed in the last years, we study lightlike singularities of variational solutions to the prescribed Lorentzian mean curvature equation with possibly unbounded (rough) curvature. This corresponds to allowing for unbounded charges in the Born-Infeld model.

papers.title: Macroscopic scalar curvature bounds on surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized Geroch conjecture, and the corresponding hyperbolic conjecture, in dimension two.
